package main
/*
#include \"hello.h\" 
*/

import \"errors\"

func HelloWorld() (string, error) {

  if c == nil { return \"\", errors.New(\"nil\") }

}

## Key Concepts
- CGO memory boundaries
- Safe preallocated buffers
- Error propagation
- Concurrency with CGO

## Why This Is Asked
CGOA bridges are common in practice when external C libraries need Go callbacks. This tests safe lifetimes, non-Go-pointer transfer, and cross-language threading.

## Key Concepts
- runtime/cgo.Handle
- //exported Go functions
- passing uintptr_t to C
- proper cleanup and synchronization

## Code Example
```c
/* header */
void register_callback(void (*cb)(int, void*), void* ctx);
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to avoid deadlocks when callbacks re-enter?
- How to handle panics in the Go callback across threads?
